correctness.rationale: A connected dominating set must select at least two from each shore, since with only b_j selected the necessary a_j is isolated in the induced subgraph. Any p,q>=2 dominate all omissions. When one shore has >=3 selections, pairwise selected vertices on other shore share a selected neighbor and connectivity follows; when p=q=2, exactly P=Q gives two disconnected matching edges. Hence all and only binomial(n,2) exceptional degree-4 sets must be excluded from the square binomial enumerator. Independently enumerated every vertex subset with literal induced-connectivity/dominating tests for n=3,4,5,6, matching every coefficient (n=3 counts 6,6,1 by sizes 4..6; n=4 counts 30,48,28,8,1). This is an infinite proof from the cases, not an extrapolation of the finite experiment.
residual_risks: All-parameter proof is combinatorial and assumes simple undirected crown graph with perfect matching deleted; it does not cover unequal shores or partial matching deletions.

evidence: Complete-bipartite polynomial allows singleton selected shores; Cr_n imposes two-per-shore and a separate matched-4-set exclusion.
